title: Okapi BM25
text: Okapi BM25 is a ranking function that saturates term frequency with parameter k1 and punishes long documents with parameter b. Rare terms earn a larger inverse document frequency.

title: The forest okapi
text: The okapi is a shy forest animal with a long tongue and zebra striped legs. It eats leaves in the dark. Visitors confuse the name with a scoring formula.

title: Spikes and weights
text: Term frequency counts how often a word appears in a document. Inverse document frequency shrinks words that show up everywhere and boosts unusual terms.

title: Ramen ramen ramen
text: ramen ramen ramen ramen ramen ramen ramen ramen. The stall sign repeats itself and hides the recipe.

title: Shoyu ramen bowl
text: A shoyu ramen bowl is soy sauce broth, noodles, and a sheet of nori. The cook names ramen once and broth once and means both.

title: Tonkotsu the opaque broth
text: Tonkotsu is an opaque white broth made by boiling pork bones for many hours until the stock turns milky and rich. The bowl is famous after midnight.

title: Street chant
text: Milky pork bone soup. Milky pork bone soup. Milky pork bone soup. Milky pork bone soup.

title: Miso soup
text: Miso soup builds on a dashi base, fermented soybean paste, tofu, and wakame. It is a thin bowl for a cold walk home.

title: Dashi the clear stock
text: Dashi is a clear Japanese stock of kombu kelp and katsuobushi smoked bonito. It is delicate and it underpins miso soup. The bowl stays clear, never milky.

title: Chashu pork
text: Chashu is rolled pork belly, braised in soy until tender, then sliced over noodles. A topping, separate from the liquid in the bowl.

title: Spill on the counter
text: Milky soup. Bleach bleach bleach ammonia. Milky soup across the counter, bleach in the fumes.

title: Two stances one match
text: Hybrid retrieval runs a sparse ranker beside a dense ranker and then applies fusion to the two lists. A document either stance places near the top can survive the cut.

title: Reciprocal rank fusion
text: Reciprocal rank fusion scores a document as one divided by k plus its rank in each list. Order is the only signal. Raw scores stay in their own units. Fusion stays calm when rankers speak different units.

title: Two towers
text: A bi-encoder embeds the query and the document in separate towers that share weights, then compares the vectors with cosine. Documents can be embedded before a question arrives.

title: The rerank stare
text: A cross-encoder reads the query and the document together. The joint read is slower and sharper, so it reranks only the top candidates from a fast first stage.

title: Feature dojo
text: Ranking features turn a document into numbers a model can weigh: lexical score, embedding cosine, title overlap, phrase match, and length. Drop one feature and measure the ranking again.

title: Say it another way
text: Query expansion adds terms a searcher left unsaid, then the second pass runs on the richer query. This is how a keyword index survives a vocabulary gap.

title: Feedback from the top
text: Pseudo relevance feedback assumes the first results are mostly right, pulls distinctive terms from them, and runs the query again. When the first pass is wrong, feedback amplifies the mistake.

title: Query expressions
text: A query expression is a small boolean tree. Terms, quoted phrases, AND, OR, and NOT compile to operations over posting lists. Phrases need token positions, counts alone miss adjacency.

title: The query log
text: Query logs record what people typed, what they clicked, and how they reformulated after a miss. A reformulation is a label the searcher wrote for free.

title: The long document penalty
text: A long document that mentions a query term once should lose to a short document that is about the term. Parameter b in BM25 sets how hard length is punished.

title: Sparse encoding
text: Sparse encoding stores a document as weights on the terms it contains. Most dimensions stay zero. Sparsity is why an inverted index can skip almost every document.

title: Inverted index
text: An inverted index maps each term to the posting list of documents that contain it, with counts and positions. Retrieval walks those lists instead of rereading the archive.

title: Graded relevance
text: Normalized discounted cumulative gain rewards a highly relevant document and discounts one you buried. A perfect order scores one. A relevant document at rank ten barely helps.

title: The vocabulary gap
text: Searchers and authors use different words for one idea. A dense encoder that has seen paraphrases can still match them. A pure keyword index misses the gap.

title: Why relevance pays rent
text: On a question answering platform the generator answers from the documents you retrieved. A wrong top document becomes a wrong answer. Relevance work shows up as answer quality.

title: Language models inside search
text: Language models rewrite queries, judge rankings, and draft answers from retrieved documents. They sit beside the index and leave the first stage retriever in place.

title: Stall license sku1844
text: Inventory code sku1844 is painted on the barley tea crate by the east gate. The clerk files it under permits rather than recipes.
